notes: Retrieved from SIMBAD on 2026-08-24T04:23:02+00:00; upstream record id: * zet01 UMa; otype: SB*.; Mizar (zeta UMa, SIMBAD main id "* zet01 UMa", the bright, historically famous naked-eye/telescopic double component of the Mizar-Alcor system) was found missing from the catalog (issue #213, Tier 2): RECONS's "100 nearest star systems" list is a research-consortium census weighted toward faint red/white dwarfs needing dedicated parallax work, and systematically misses evolved/luminous nearby stars whose distances were already well-established by other means (the same gap identified for Fomalhaut in issue #207). Not present in data/raw/recons/candidate_stars.json under any query form and not one of that batch's documented unresolved_stars.json entries either - a transcription gap in the original RECONS source list, not a resolution failure. Note: the plain query "Mizar" returns zero rows from SIMBAD once the V (apparent magnitude) votable field is requested - an upstream join quirk specific to that alias, confirmed by testing each votable field individually - so this record was resolved via SIMBAD's own preferred main identifier for the bright, visible component, "zet01 UMa" (aliases include "NAME Mizar A"), which resolves cleanly with full photometry. Added here as a standalone, honestly-tagged gap-fill (group.secondary: ["nearby-bright-star-gap-fill"]) via the same SimbadResolver/acquire mechanism, not as a claimed member of the original RECONS-nearest-100 candidate batch - see data/raw/gap_fills/README.md.
